messages:
alex: Quick heads-up — ran into inconsistent error codes on /v1/generate today. Some client SDKs saw 500s when the payload had an unknown field (`temperature_mode`) instead of 4xx. Can we decide a contract?

simon: Ugh, thanks for flagging. Can you paste minimal repro (request + response)?

alex: Yep — repro below. Server currently returns 500 and no structured error.
```json
POST /v1/generate
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-base-1",
  "prompt": "summarize: ...",
  "temperature_mode": "high",
  "max_tokens": 512
}
```
response (current):
```json
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
<html>some stack trace</html>
```
\nmaria: That should definitely be a 4xx. Unknown top-level fields = client mistake. I'd prefer 400 for malformed/invalid shape and 422 for semantic errors (e.g., prompt too long).

simon: Agreed on the split. Quick proposal:
- 400 = parse errors / incorrect field types / unknown top-level fields
- 422 = resource/semantic validation (lengths, incompatible params, model-specific limits)
- 429 = rate limiting / quota
- 409 = idempotency conflict when `Idempotency-Key` reused with different payload
- 5xx = infra/runtime failures only (and include retryable=true)

alex: +1. Also we need a standard error envelope so SDKs can map retryability. Suggest something like: 
```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid_request",
    "status": 400,
    "message": "unknown field: temperature_mode",
    "field": "temperature_mode",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

maria: Looks good. For 5xx responses we should set `retryable: true` when it's a transient DB/connectivity failure and false for terminal runtime errors (e.g. model compilation failure). Runtime should be able to decide.

infra-bot: note: added incident template for repeated 500s. ticket INF-482 created.

simon: Small nuance: streaming endpoints (SSE / chunked) — if we hit a validation midstream (e.g., client sends midstream update that violates allowed tokens), do we send a 4xx event and close or a 5xx? My preference: if the error is client-originated (bad update) emit a terminal error event with 4xx and close. If server dies midstream, emit error event with 5xx and `retryable: true` header so clients can fallback.

alex: Implementation note: our preflight validation currently runs only on initial chunk for streaming; we should validate every control update. I'll open a small PR to run `validateParams()` on each control chunk.

maria: Also call out idempotency: if a retry comes with the same `Idempotency-Key` but different payload, return 409 with an explanation and include the stored request fingerprint.

simon: For backward compatibility: older SDKs expect plain text 500 for unknowns. We should make this non-breaking by:
1) starting to send proper 4xx/422 with the new envelope
2) for a month, also set header `X-Redwood-Legacy-Error: true` on responses that mirror old behavior? Hmm maybe not ideal. Alternate: emit warning logs and a migration page in the changelog + client SDK patch.

linda: Can we add a clear migration note in /docs/api/errors and a short snippet for SDK teams? I can draft.

alex: Action items: 
- simon to add server validation for unknown fields -> return 400 + envelope (PR: repo/runtime #2034) — assigned simon
- alex to add streaming mid-chunk validate + SSE error event shape PR -> #2035
- linda to draft docs + changelog blurb
- infra-bot ticket INF-482 for follow-up on current 500s

simon: I'll do a tiny unit test matrix: unknown field -> 400, bad type -> 400, prompt too long -> 422, idempotency mismatch -> 409. Will include RFC link in PR comments.

maria: One last: please include the `error.code` enums in the PR (e.g., `invalid_request`, `invalid_parameter`, `rate_limit`, `idempotency_conflict`, `server_error`). SDKs will map to retry/backoff easily.

alex: sweet. pinging @simon for the PR when ready. :thumbsup:

simon: will post PR in ~1h.

linda: thanks team, will start the docs draft and ping when done. :sparkles:

infra-bot: INF-482 updated: root cause tagged as "missing validation for unknown fields".

alex: thanks — that should clean up the noisy 500s and make client behavior deterministic.
